 # Data Model: Support Ticket Triage Assistant
 
 This feature is stateless: one ticket is processed per invocation and no application data is persisted. The shapes below describe runtime values and, where noted, human-owned evaluation data.
 
 ## Ticket
 
 | Field | Type | Constraints |
 |---|---|---|
 | `text` | `str` | Raw plain-text customer message; input is not trimmed. `text.strip() == ""` or `len(text) > 4000` is rejected before model setup. Python `len` counts Unicode code points. |
 
 The CLI starts from file bytes, decodes strict UTF-8 without newline translation, and removes exactly one leading U+FEFF before creating the ticket text. (FR-001–FR-003, FR-012–FR-013, GR-001)
 
 ## Triage decision
 
 A JSON object represented by a Python dictionary with exactly these six keys:
 
 | Key | Type / allowed values | Triage | Clarify | Refuse |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | `action` | string: `triage`, `clarify`, `refuse` | `triage` | `clarify` | `refuse` |
 | `category` | string: `billing`, `technical`, `account_access`, `shipping`, `other`; otherwise null | required | null | null |
 | `priority` | string: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent`; otherwise null | required | null | null |
 | `summary` | string of 1–200 code points; otherwise null | required | null | null |
 | `clarification_question` | string of 5–200 code points ending in `?`; otherwise null | null | required | null |
 | `refusal_reason` | string: `invalid_input`, `prompt_injection`, `not_a_support_ticket`; otherwise null | null | null | required |
 
 Action and field presence/nullability must be consistent. Only the local deterministic guard can produce `invalid_input`; a model reply with that value is invalid. All output strings are checked for a 13-or-more ASCII digit run after spaces and hyphens are removed, an API-key-pattern match (`sk-` plus at least 20 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen characters), and literal `OPENAI_API_KEY`. (FR-002, FR-004–FR-011; INV-001–INV-007; GR-002–GR-005)
 
 ## Model reply and errors
 
 | Entity | Fields / behavior |
 |---|---|
 | Model reply | Exact raw string returned by `ModelClient.complete(system, user)`. It must be strict JSON that parses into a valid decision; duplicates, constants such as `NaN`, extra/missing keys, malformed JSON, and any invariant violation invalidate it. |
 | `InvalidModelOutput` | Exception for every invalid raw reply. Its `raw_reply` attribute is the exact original string. Do not sanitize or rewrite this diagnostic value; CLI must never print it. |
 | `ServiceError` | Exception for service/configuration/network errors. The fixed message is exactly `Model service unavailable.` and it contains no underlying error, API key, or cause. |
 
 (FR-009–FR-011; INV-001–INV-007)
 
 ## Evaluation case and evaluation result (human-owned)
 
 These are specification-defined entities for `evals/` only; they do not imply creation or modification of evaluation files in this plan.
 
 | Entity | Required content and validation |
 |---|---|
 | Evaluation case | Unique id, input text, tags, gold action, and traces of applicable FR/INV/GR ids. Triage cases also include gold category, gold priority, and key terms. Refusal cases include gold refusal reason. `forbidden_terms`, if present, must be checked case-insensitively against every output string field. |
 | Per-case result | Case status and score. A contract/invariant/guardrail failure or wrong action yields `FAIL`, score 0. `InvalidModelOutput` is `FAIL`, one attempt, score 0, with independent Layers 1 and 2 run on its exact raw reply. A service failure after up to three attempts is `ERROR`, excluded from the aggregate. |
 | Evaluation run | Arithmetic mean of scored cases and final `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `INVALID`. Any `ERROR` makes the run `INVALID`. A `PASS` requires all contract/invariant checks, all guardrail cases passing, and aggregate score at least 0.85. |
 
 (FR-014–FR-019; EV-001–EV-004)
 
 ## Relationships and state
 
 `Ticket` → one `ModelClient` request (except deterministic guard refusals) → one raw `Model reply` → either one validated `Triage decision` or one explicit exception. There is no persisted state. The independent evaluator may process a dataset case once per run and may retry service failures up to two times, but retry policy does not belong to the library or OpenAI client.

 # Interface Contracts
 
 The public library and CLI are separate entry points over one service. The model protocol is injectable so callers and human-owned tests can control model replies without network access (NFR-001).
 
 ## Library
 
 ```text
 triage(ticket_text: str, client: ModelClient | None = None) -> dict
 ModelClient.complete(system: str, user: str) -> str
 ```
 
 - Check the deterministic guard first. Empty/whitespace-only or over-4000-code-point input returns the six-key `invalid_input` refusal with zero client creation, environment lookup, or model calls.
 - For other input, use the injected client or create `OpenAIClient`; send the fixed loaded system prompt and the exact ticket text as the user message.
 - Parse and validate the raw reply with the complete decision contract. Return validated values unchanged, or raise `InvalidModelOutput` with exact `raw_reply`.
 - Raise `ServiceError` for model configuration/service errors. Its message is exactly `Model service unavailable.`.
 
 ## Decision JSON object
 
 Every successful library result has exactly these keys: `action`, `category`, `priority`, `summary`, `clarification_question`, and `refusal_reason`. Types, enums, action-dependent nullability, code-point length rules, refusal provenance, and sensitive-pattern exclusions are defined in [data-model.md](../data-model.md) and the approved [specification](../spec.md) (FR-004–FR-011; INV-001–INV-007).
 
 The reply parser does not accept duplicate object keys (at any depth), non-standard JSON constants, non-object JSON, missing or extra keys, wrong types/enums, or any invariant violation. It performs no repair, inference, or normalization.
 
 ## OpenAI adapter
 
 `OpenAIClient.complete(system, user)`:
 
 1. Read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` at call time; strip only to determine whether each is missing/empty. If either is empty, raise `ServiceError` before network activity.
 2. Construct the official client with `api_key=...`, `timeout=30.0`, and `max_retries=0`.
 3. Call Chat Completions with one system message, one user message, and `response_format={"type":"json_object"}`. Do not set temperature or strict structured outputs.
 4. Return the response content string, or `""` if content is `None`.
 5. Catch only `openai.OpenAIError` and raise the fixed `ServiceError` with no chained underlying cause. Do not log, print, or expose credentials or SDK error text.
 
 The model itself must produce the JSON-object response specified in `prompts/system.md`; independent contract parsing remains mandatory.
 
 ## CLI
 
 ```text
 main(argv: list[str], client: ModelClient | None = None) -> int
 ```
 
 - Exactly one argument is required. Do not interpret options.
 - Read the named file as bytes; strict UTF-8 decode with no newline translation; remove one leading U+FEFF if present; then invoke `triage`.
 - Successful decisions, including refusals, are serialized as `json.dumps(decision, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)` encoded UTF-8, followed by exactly `b"\n"` on `sys.stdout.buffer`. Exit 0.
 - Failures write no stdout bytes and exactly one LF-terminated message to `sys.stderr.buffer`:
 
 | Condition | Exit | Stderr line |
 |---|---:|---|
 | Argument count is not one | 2 | `error: expected exactly one input file path` |
 | Missing, directory, unreadable file, or invalid UTF-8 | 2 | `error: cannot read input file` |
 | `ServiceError` | 3 | `error: model service unavailable` |
 | `InvalidModelOutput` | 4 | `error: model returned an invalid response` |
 
 The CLI must not print raw invalid replies or any partial/success-shaped JSON on error (FR-012–FR-013).
 
 ## Executable entry point and configuration
 
 `python -m ticket_triage` may load key/value entries from an untracked `.env` file in the Part-1B root via `env_loader.py`, setting only environment names not already set, then call `cli.main`. The library modules never read `.env`. The plan has not opened or read any `.env` file. Only `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` are consumed by the OpenAI adapter.

 # Research: Support Ticket Triage Assistant
 
 All requirements supplied for this feature are sufficiently specific; there are no unresolved technical-context questions. This research records the fixed decisions and the relevant SDK integration guidance. It does not change the approved specification.
 
 ## Python runtime and dependency boundary
 
 **Decision**: Use Python 3.12+ and the official `openai` package as the only third-party runtime dependency. Use the standard library for JSON handling, regular expressions, environment access, file I/O, and CLI serialization.
 
 **Rationale**: The runtime version and dependency boundary are explicit in the feature input and constitution (V). Separating the dependency behind `ModelClient` allows deterministic tests and avoids requiring network access for library tests (NFR-001).
 
 **Alternatives considered**: Third-party schema, CLI, retry, and dotenv libraries were not selected because the contract and behavior are fully defined and the dependency budget excludes them. No package or requirements manifest is in scope.
 
 ## OpenAI client integration
 
 **Decision**: Implement `OpenAIClient.complete()` with the official SDK's `OpenAI` client, configured at call time with `api_key`, `timeout=30.0`, and `max_retries=0`. Use Chat Completions with a system message and exact ticket user message, plus `response_format={"type":"json_object"}`. Do not send a temperature parameter and do not request strict structured outputs. Map only `openai.OpenAIError` to `ServiceError` using `raise ... from None`; do not log or expose the original exception. Return an empty string when the response message content is `None`.
 
 **Rationale**: These request parameters and error semantics are fixed by the feature input and implement FR-003, FR-009–FR-010, and AC-019–AC-020/AC-050–AC-051. Official SDK documentation confirms support for a client API key, timeout configuration, disabling automatic retries with `max_retries=0`, Chat Completions, optional `response_format`, and an optional temperature parameter. `json_object` provides JSON mode rather than schema enforcement, which preserves the requirement that the independent validator detect violations (FR-009).
 
 **Alternatives considered**: Responses API and strict structured outputs are not selected because the requested interface explicitly requires Chat Completions and JSON mode without strict outputs. SDK retries are disabled because the evaluator controls its own maximum of three attempts (FR-019). Passing an explicit temperature is unnecessary and forbidden by the feature input.
 
 **Official references**:
 
 - [openai-python README: supported Python and Chat Completions](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/README.md)
 - [openai-python README: retries and timeouts](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/README.md#retries)
 - [Chat Completions create parameters](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/chat/completion_create_params.py)
 - [JSON response format parameter](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/shared_params/response_format_json_object.py)
 - [OpenAI JSON mode and structured outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs)
 - [OpenAI Python SDK exception definitions](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/_exceptions.py)
 
 **Caveat**: Current OpenAI guidance recommends the Responses API for new integrations, while the SDK documents Chat Completions as supported. This design retains Chat Completions because it is an explicit requirement, not an open choice.
 
 ## Strict JSON parsing and contract validation
 
 **Decision**: Use standard-library `json.loads` with an `object_pairs_hook` that rejects duplicate keys in every object and a `parse_constant` callback that rejects `NaN` and infinities. Validate the parsed value and every decision invariant without repairs or normalization; on any failure, raise `InvalidModelOutput` containing the exact unmodified reply.
 
 **Rationale**: The specification makes exact structure and raw-reply preservation acceptance requirements (FR-009, INV-001–INV-007, AC-008–AC-018, AC-030–AC-035, AC-046–AC-049, AC-056). This approach uses only the standard library and keeps the parser deterministic and independent of the model.
 
 **Alternatives considered**: JSON Schema or automatic output repair were rejected. A schema dependency violates the runtime dependency constraint, while repair would hide model violations and is explicitly prohibited.
 
 ## Input and command-line handling
 
 **Decision**: Count Python string code points with `len`; reject blank text using `strip()` only for the blank check, without changing the original input; read CLI input as bytes, decode strict UTF-8, remove one initial BOM, and write compact sorted UTF-8 JSON bytes plus one LF.
 
 **Rationale**: These choices directly encode the Unicode clarifications, boundary cases, and exact CLI stream requirements (FR-002, FR-012–FR-013, AC-001–AC-004, AC-022–AC-027, AC-044–AC-045, AC-055).
 
 **Alternatives considered**: Text-mode file reading and newline translation were rejected because they could alter CR/LF boundaries. Trimming ticket text was rejected because length must be measured on the original text.
 
 ## Evaluation ownership
 
 **Decision**: Document evaluation behavior and AC traceability but leave the dataset, evaluator, tests, and harness to the human engineer.
 
 **Rationale**: The spec requires an independent evaluator (FR-014–FR-019, EV-001–EV-004), while the constitution explicitly reserves `tests/`, `evals/`, and `.harness/` for the human engineer. No such files are created by this plan.
 
 **Alternatives considered**: Generating evaluator/test artifacts as part of this plan was rejected because it violates the stated ownership boundary.

 # Quickstart and Validation Guide
 
 This guide describes how the human engineer can validate the implementation after the runtime package and human-owned test/evaluation components exist. It does not create tests, evaluation data, or harness files.
 
 ## Prerequisites
 
 - Python 3.12 or later.
 - The official `openai` package installed in the active environment for a live model call.
 - For live calls only, nonempty `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` values. Do not place credentials in source control or evidence.
 - The human-owned test and evaluation components required by the approved specification.
 
 The library and CLI support an injected fake `ModelClient`, so deterministic contract and CLI checks do not require credentials or network access.
 
 ## Run the CLI
 
 From the Part-1B project root in PowerShell, configure the source package path and model settings, then pass one existing UTF-8 ticket file:
 
 ```powershell
 $env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
 $env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "<configured-key>"
 $env:OPENAI_MODEL = "<configured-model>"
 python -m ticket_triage .\ticket.txt
 ```
 
 Expected behavior: one compact JSON object followed by one LF on success. A blank ticket returns the deterministic `invalid_input` refusal without requiring either model variable. CLI errors have empty stdout and the exact stderr line/exit code in [interfaces.md](./contracts/interfaces.md).
 
 ## Validate deterministic behavior
 
 Run the human-owned unit tests with the test runner configured by the engineer. They should use an injected fake client to verify the guard boundaries (empty, whitespace-only, 4000, 4001 code points), exact user-message preservation, system-prompt stability, contract rejection, exception data, and CLI bytes/status.
 
 The acceptance-criterion-to-component mapping is in [acceptance-traceability.md](./contracts/acceptance-traceability.md). In particular, verify duplicate-key and non-finite JSON rejection, exact raw-reply preservation, 12/13-digit and API-key-pattern boundaries, BOM removal, CR/LF counting, UTF-8 non-ASCII serialization, and zero output on CLI error.
 
 ## Validate the independent evaluation
 
 The human-owned evaluation must validate its dataset and then apply Layers 1–3 as specified in the feature spec (FR-014–FR-019; EV-001–EV-004). Verify independently that Layers 1 and 2 run for returned decisions and exact raw replies in `InvalidModelOutput`, service errors are retried up to three total attempts, and an unresolved service error makes the run `INVALID`. Do not add or modify evaluator components as part of this plan.
 
 ## Reference contracts
 
 - Runtime entity shapes and invariants: [data-model.md](./data-model.md)
 - Library, model adapter, and CLI behavior: [interfaces.md](./contracts/interfaces.md)
 - Every acceptance criterion's implementation and human-owned verification location: [acceptance-traceability.md](./contracts/acceptance-traceability.md)

 # Support Ticket Triage Assistant Constitution
 
 ## Core Principles
 
 ### I. Modular Boundaries and Secret Isolation
 The library MUST separate deterministic input guarding, prompt construction, the model-client
 interface, response parsing and validation, and the thin command-line layer. Prompt text MUST
 reside in files under `prompts/`, never in source code. All network access and application reading
 of the API key MUST be confined to one small OpenAI client module behind the model-client
 interface, so tests can inject a fake client. The key MUST come from `OPENAI_API_KEY` and the
 model name from `OPENAI_MODEL`. The command-line layer and harness MAY load these values from an
 untracked `.env` file. The values MUST NOT appear in source, logs, error messages, or output.
 
 ### II. Untrusted Input and Deterministic Guardrails
 Ticket text MUST be treated as untrusted data: it MUST never be executed or used as a file path,
 command, or tool argument, and MUST NOT change application instructions or the output schema.
 The deterministic input guard MUST reject empty, whitespace-only, and oversized input before any
 model call; each such refusal MUST make zero model calls.
 
 ### III. Validated Triage Contract and Explicit Failures
 The output MUST conform to the output schema contract defined in the specification. Responses
 MUST be parsed and validated against that contract before they are returned as triage decisions.
 Network, timeout, rate-limit, authentication, and other model or service failures MUST raise a
 distinct error type and MUST never be represented as a triage result.
 
 ### IV. Independent Evaluation and Acceptance
 An independent evaluation harness MUST decide acceptance. Acceptance requires 100 percent schema
 validity, 100 percent structural-invariant compliance, 100 percent pass on guardrail cases, and
 an aggregate score at or above the threshold and scoring formula stated in the specification
 before evaluation begins. A language-model judge MAY contribute to aggregate scoring, but MUST
 NOT replace schema validation or invariant checks.
 
 ### V. Minimal Dependencies and Maintainability
 The runtime MUST use Python 3.12 or later and the official `openai` package as its only
 third-party runtime dependency. Solutions MUST prefer simple, maintainable implementations over
 unnecessary complexity.
 
 ## Technical Constraints
 
 Development tools MAY include `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `ruff`, `bandit`, and `jsonschema`. The
 harness MAY populate `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` from an untracked `.env` file; `.env`
 files MUST NOT be committed. API keys and credentials MUST NOT be committed or written to
 evidence or logs.
 
 ## Evaluation and Scope Controls
 
 Before any evaluation, the specification MUST define the output schema contract, structural
 invariants, behavioral properties, guardrail rules, evaluation threshold, and scoring formula.
 Every acceptance criterion and invariant in the specification MUST map to at least one test or
 evaluation case.
 
 The independent harness MUST enforce all of the following deterministic-code quality standards:
 
 - `ruff` reports zero errors.
 - `bandit` reports zero medium- or high-severity findings.
 - All deterministic tests pass.
 - Line coverage of `src/` is at least 90 percent, excluding only the thin OpenAI client module,
   which is exercised by the live evaluation.
 
 The `tests/`, `evals/`, and `.harness/` directories are owned by the human engineer and are
 outside the scope of Spec Kit implementation tasks. Generated task lists MUST NOT include tasks
 to create or modify those directories, though tasks MAY reference them for traceability. During
 implementation and repair, the coding agent MAY change only `src/` and `prompts/`. It MUST NOT
 modify the specification, `tests/`, `evals/`, or `.harness/`; delete or weaken tests, assertions,

 # Implementation Plan: Support Ticket Triage Assistant
 
 **Branch**: `001-support-ticket-triage` | **Date**: 2026-11-03 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
 
 **Input**: Approved feature specification and implementation constraints supplied for this plan.
 
 ## Summary
 
 Build a Python 3.12+ library and one-file command-line tool that turn a single customer ticket into a validated six-field triage decision. A deterministic guard handles empty, whitespace-only, and over-limit text before any model configuration or network access. Other tickets are sent unchanged as user data alongside one invariant system prompt to an injectable model client. The raw JSON reply is strictly parsed and validated; invalid output and service failures remain distinct, sanitized errors. The CLI handles strict UTF-8 file input and byte-exact output. The official `openai` package is the sole third-party runtime dependency. See [research.md](./research.md) for decisions and [contracts/interfaces.md](./contracts/interfaces.md) for public interfaces.
 
 ## Technical Context
 
 **Language/Version**: Python 3.12+
 
 **Primary Dependencies**: Official `openai` Python package only at runtime; standard library for all other runtime behavior.
 
 **Storage**: None. Input is one file for the CLI; no application persistence.
 
 **Testing**: Human-owned tests and evaluation components specified in the approved spec. `tests/`, `evals/`, and `.harness/` are not generated or modified by this plan.
 
 **Target Platform**: Python 3.12+ environments with access to the configured OpenAI service when model-assisted triage is required.
 
 **Project Type**: Python library plus command-line interface.
 
 **Performance Goals**: No latency or throughput target is specified. The OpenAI client timeout is 30 seconds; deterministic checks are local.
 
 **Constraints**: Exactly one third-party runtime dependency; fixed six-key contract; Unicode code-point length counting; no response repair; sanitized service errors; no output of specified sensitive patterns; the system prompt is identical for each ticket. No project/dependency manifest, tests, evals, or harness files are in scope. `.env` files must not be opened or read during this planning task.
 
 **Scale/Scope**: One ticket per library or CLI invocation; no history, persistence, attachments, UI, or multi-ticket processing.
 
 ## Constitution Check
 
 ### Pre-design gate
 
 | Principle / constraint | Plan decision | Status |
 |---|---|---|
 | I. Modular boundaries and secret isolation | Separate guard, prompt loading, model protocol/client, contract parsing, service orchestration, CLI, and optional `__main__` environment loading. Only `openai_client.py` reads model credentials and performs network activity. | PASS |
 | II. Untrusted input and deterministic guardrails | Treat the user message strictly as ticket data; reject invalid length/blank input before client creation or environment access. | PASS |
 | III. Validated contract and explicit failures | Validate every raw reply without normalization; distinguish `InvalidModelOutput` from fixed-message `ServiceError`. | PASS |
 | IV. Independent evaluation and acceptance | Keep the human-owned evaluation harness independent; map every AC in [acceptance-traceability.md](./contracts/acceptance-traceability.md). Do not produce or change evaluation files. | PASS |
 | V. Minimal dependencies and maintainability | Python 3.12+, official `openai` package only at runtime, otherwise standard library; use direct, small modules. | PASS |
 | Evaluation and scope controls | Do not create or alter `tests/`, `evals/`, or `.harness/`; no change to thresholds or harness behavior. | PASS |
 
 No violations or complexity exceptions are required.
 
 ### Post-design gate
 
 The proposed package and prompt tree preserves the boundaries and constraints above. Runtime secrets remain isolated to the OpenAI client; deterministic input refusals need no configuration. Evaluation traces are documentation only and point to human-owned components. The generated plan artifacts stay under `specs/001-support-ticket-triage/`. **Result: PASS; no unresolved clarifications.**
 
 ## Architecture and Key Decisions
 
 1. **Small, injectable module boundaries**: `guard.py` performs deterministic input validation; `contract.py` is pure parsing and invariant validation; `model_client.py` defines the replaceable protocol; `openai_client.py` owns environment reads and network access; `service.py` composes them; `cli.py` owns argument, file, and stream behavior. This satisfies Constitution I and V, NFR-001, FR-001–FR-002, FR-009–FR-013, and INV-001–INV-007.
 2. **Input gate precedes all external state**: The service checks exactly `text.strip() == ""` or `len(text) > 4000` without trimming the original ticket. It returns the deterministic `invalid_input` decision without creating a default client or reading environment configuration. This implements FR-002, FR-008, GR-001, and AC-001–AC-004/AC-045.
 3. **Fixed prompt and untrusted user message**: Load `prompts/system.md` relative to the package location and send it unchanged for each call; pass the exact ticket text only as the user message. The prompt requires the JSON contract and addresses categories, priority, ambiguity, refusals, prompt injection, embedded instructions, and prohibited output. This implements FR-003–FR-007, GR-002–GR-005, and AC-021/AC-036–AC-038.
 4. **Strict contract; no repair**: Decode with `json.loads`, reject duplicate keys at every object depth via `object_pairs_hook`, reject non-standard constants via `parse_constant`, and validate exact keys, types, enums, action-field consistency, lengths, refusal provenance, and prohibited patterns. Raise `InvalidModelOutput` with the exact original string on every failure. This implements FR-009, FR-011, INV-001–INV-007, and SC-001/SC-003.
 5. **Explicit OpenAI adapter and safe service errors**: Create the client inside `complete()` after verifying stripped, nonempty `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL`; configure 30-second timeout and no SDK retries; make one Chat Completions JSON-object request without a temperature override. Return `""` for null content. Catch only `openai.OpenAIError` and raise `ServiceError` with no cause or underlying text. This implements FR-010, NFR-001, and AC-019–AC-020/AC-050–AC-051. Evaluation retries, where applicable, belong to the separate human-owned evaluator (FR-019), not the library client.
 6. **Byte-defined CLI behavior**: Accept exactly one path, read bytes, strictly decode UTF-8 without newline translation, remove one leading U+FEFF, then call the same library function. Serialize with sorted keys, compact separators, and `ensure_ascii=False`; write UTF-8 plus one LF to the binary stream. Catch only the specified service/contract errors at the CLI boundary and map file/argument failures separately. This implements FR-012–FR-013 and AC-022–AC-029/AC-044–AC-045/AC-055.
 7. **Evaluation remains independently owned**: The specification’s dataset, scoring, retries, and run status requirements are traced to the human-owned `evals/` components. This plan neither implements nor creates evaluation or test files, consistent with Constitution IV and its scope controls. FR-014–FR-019, EV-001–EV-004, and AC-039–AC-043/AC-052–AC-054 are verification references only.
 8. **Optional `.env` convenience belongs only to the executable entry point**: `env_loader.py` may parse key/value lines when `__main__.py` starts, setting only variables not already present. Library calls do not load `.env`. No `.env` file is opened, read, printed, or modified during planning. This respects Constitution I and FR-010.
